question: Were there more CPUC ignitions in PG&E or SCE territory in 2020 compared to 2023, and by how much did each change?
label: answer
answer_text: In the CPUC-ignitions dataset, PG&E had more utility-attributed ignitions than SCE in both 2020 (510 vs. 145) and 2023 (374 vs. 90). From 2020 to 2023, PG&E decreased by 136 ignitions and SCE decreased by 55. These are utility-caused or utility-attributed counts, not all-cause wildfire counts; they differ from counts spatially contained within each utility’s territory (PG&E: 509 in 2020 and 377 in 2023; SCE: 145 and 87).

question: Were there more wildfire incidents in 2021 or 2022?
label: answer
answer_text: The CAL FIRE incident-map feed recorded 172 Wildfire/Fire incidents in 2021 and 150 in 2022, so it recorded more in 2021. These counts include only records classified as Wildfire/Fire; 1,234 records have no incident type. The feed is not CAL FIRE’s Redbook census, and count-based year-to-year comparisons are not reliable measures of changes in fire occurrence.

qualifications.text: CAL FIRE has 1,234 records without incident type and 282 without utility tags; default counts include only Wildfire/Fire incident types.

CAL FIRE rows in this warehouse are the fire.ca.gov incident-map feed, not CAL FIRE's Redbook census. The map's posting threshold dropped in 2024 (median acreage 70 to 43; sub-100-acre incidents 71 to 422). The 133 to 611 Wildfire/Fire count change is a posting change, not a change in fire occurrence. Acreage totals in the feed track the Redbook at 95–97% in both years, so acre-based comparisons remain valid; count-based year-to-year comparisons do not.
